![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/cf2c500974f9c88751b9dec98cc53b5d3616b736f3ab0504adae5879cac2001a.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $y=2{x}^{2}-2x$ and $y=3-3{x}^{2}$ for $x\in [-\frac{3}{5},1]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=5.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
Let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/d5593e8c1e1d544acb8824d9428823d3d6cef3971a1cedd4b087a7902b0e2239.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=3-3{x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y=2{x}^{2}-2x.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=2{x}^{2}-2x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/bddc78f683e28ec6e97fddb32f95dfdaaff27d3aafbdfc61f424857916f81a6c.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}[\,(5)-(2{x}^{2}-2x)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}{[5-2{x}^{2}+2x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=3-3{x}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/cc049c46593baf1d96c04b95680d6b444ab9ceffc64d1f23f310f70e78684c14.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}[\,(5)-(3-3{x}^{2})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}{[2+3{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}{[5-2{x}^{2}+2x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}{[2+3{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-3/5}^{1}({[5-2{x}^{2}+2x]}^{2}-{[2+3{x}^{2}]}^{2})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
